title: Block close: reason and faith
hook: Maimonides shows reason can serve faith

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: thought and deed. A law code that starts with knowing God, and a philosophy that ends in kindness. Did your thought find its pair of hands? Day one thousand one hundred seventy.

An epitaph that says none like Moses. A commentary on the Mishnah. A list of principles of faith. Chapters on the health of the soul, and a middle way. A code of law in clear Hebrew. The rungs of giving. A path of return. A picture of the messianic age. A guide for the perplexed, with silence as praise. And then the arguments, the son, the honest reading, the grave by the lake. That is the road this block has walked with one man, and one question sits underneath all of it. Can a mind that asks hard questions still stand before God? Today closes the block with his answer.
screen: `NONE LIKE MOSES.` → `ONE MAN, MANY BOOKS.` → `ONE QUESTION UNDERNEATH.`

segments.voice: Block close: reason and faith. Turn Maimonides' answer four ways. First, reason is part of obeying. The Torah says the nations will hear these laws and call Israel "a wise and understanding people." Maimonides leans on that verse in the Guide: if outsiders can see the wisdom, the commandments must have reasons a mind can look for. Thinking isn't a threat to the law. It's one way of honoring it. Second, reason clears the way. You saw him do it with God's hand and God's eye: figures of speech, he said, not a body. And with praise: sometimes the truest thing a mind can offer is silence. Reason sweeps away wrong pictures so a truer reverence has room. Third, reason knows its edge. About the messianic age he said nobody will know how until it happens. About God he said we know better what God is not. A careful mind can tell where its knowing stops. Fourth, reason ends in love and in deed. His code says that a person who looks at the wonders of creation is moved to love and to awe. And his Guide ends with going out to do kindness, justice and righteousness. For Maimonides, thinking is not the opposite of faith. It is one of the ways faith is served. Not everyone agreed, then or now. You met the Rabad's sharp notes, and the Ramban's other way, which pointed toward a hidden layer in the Torah. Tomorrow a new block begins with that hidden layer: the tradition called Kabbalah, a different road into the same Torah.
screen: `A WISE AND UNDERSTANDING PEOPLE.` · `REASON CLEARS THE WAY.` · `REASON KNOWS ITS EDGE.` · `REASON ENDS IN LOVE AND DEED.` · then, large: `REASON SERVES FAITH.`

segments.voice: Take a slow breath in, and a longer one out. Pick one question you've been carrying, about faith, a choice, a person. Think it through slowly, the way Maimonides liked. What do I actually know? What am I only picturing? Where does my knowing stop? Take one step at a time, and don't rush to the end. When you reach the edge of what you can know, stop there, and let the rest be quiet. The bell holds the time.
Block close. This stretch with Maimonides ends here: reason that searches, clears away wrong pictures, knows its edge, and leads to love and deed. Today's word.
Your line: reason serves faith. Today, think one thing all the way through before you act on it, and notice where your knowing stops. Day one thousand one hundred seventy.

howItsDone: Jews study Maimonides' code and his Guide in yeshivas, universities and study groups, and his principles of faith appear in prayer books in the hymn Yigdal and the Ani Ma'amin.
